notes: The trunk reads near-vertical for the whole pull, which usually means the clip is filmed front-on rather than side-on. The angle saturates near 90° in that view and this score is not meaningful.

The two sides disagree by 9.9° on average. A steady offset means the camera is not square to the lifter (or the lifter is twisted on the bar) — real signal, not error. A jittery one means the pose track is unreliable; check the band on the plot.
Ankle extension (rising onto the toes) is not measured: ViTPose's COCO-17 output has no foot keypoint, so only two of the three joints in "triple extension" — hip and knee — are scored here.
